content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"This judge text is resolving a link-versus-challenge collision by assessing whether individual rows are answered and whether the sign's sense is open, which is the kind of assessment K-C governs for a pressing side's own chain.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] G answers the 'almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows, leaving the sign's sense open.","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse -- reading A requires comparing the pressing chain as a whole against the link by support; reading B permits deciding by individual rows or open-sense treatment. The judge text used B.","why":"The judge text treats [CR2] G as answering individual almah/bethulah and near-fulfillment rows and then uses the sign's open sense to call D5 vs C5 underdetermined, rather than weighing the pressing side's chain as a whole against the link by footing as K-C requires."}
